issue.title: 100% CPU/drop in upload speed

repository.name: rclone
repository.description: "rsync for cloud storage" - Google Drive, S3, Dropbox, Backblaze B2, One Drive, Swift, Hubic, Wasabi, Google Cloud Storage, Azure Blob, Azure Files, Yandex Files

issue.body:
> What is your rclone version (eg output from `rclone -V`)
rclone: Version "v1.34"

> Which OS you are using and how many bits (eg Windows 7, 64 bit)
Debian 8.5 64-bit

> Which cloud storage system are you using? (eg Google Drive)
Amazon Drive, crypt overlay

> The command you were trying to run (eg `rclone copy /tmp remote:tmp`)
/usr/local/bin/rclone copy --verbose --stats 0 --no-traverse "amazon:Backup/Anime" "amazon-private:Backup/Anime"

> A log from the command with the `-v` flag (eg output from `rclone -v copy /tmp remote:tmp`)
[backup-log.txt](https://github.com/ncw/rclone/files/640519/backup-log.txt)

![backup-cpu](https://cloud.githubusercontent.com/assets/49737/21026548/b1b1ad24-bd52-11e6-9eef-475966c69e02.png)

I decided (belatedly) to encrypt my Amazon Drive data. I've been using rclone to copy everything down and back up to a crypt remote. Host is a Dell R710 server with 1Gbps connection to the internet and direct peering to AWS-East. Performance really shouldn't be an issue.

After a while, I found that CPU spikes to 100% and stays there permanently, and transmit performance drops. Sometimes steadily drifts down; other times it just craters to a few KB/sec. Once CPU pegs to 100% it *never* drops back. In the attached log, 100% CPU begins at 13:05. I don't see anything that jumps out - even if retries cause some lowered network performance, nothing should cause massive CPU use like this.

A few more details - while running my first attempts yesterday I achieved consistent 500Mbps transfer, with spikes up to the full 1Gbps. Since I wasn't seeing problems yet I didn't keep any logs or debugging information, but I know my setup is certainly capable of a *lot* more. I've also tried giving the VM more CPU and memory, up to 4 vCPU (~10Ghz) and 4GB of memory - no change; rclone still manages to consume 100% of all available CPUs (390% in top, for instance) without significant upload progress. Kill rclone and restart, and as soon as it churns through all the unchanged files it transfers away merrily - until it pegs again (you can see that in the graph attached - I killed an earlier pegged session and restarted it).

Ultimately this is making rclone unusable for this task. *Should* I even be using it for this (download from amazon, encrypt, upload back to amazon)?

issue.title: Copy to ACD crypt stalls out after 100% upload.

repository.name: rclone
repository.description: "rsync for cloud storage" - Google Drive, S3, Dropbox, Backblaze B2, One Drive, Swift, Hubic, Wasabi, Google Cloud Storage, Azure Blob, Azure Files, Yandex Files

issue.body:
Previously was using the GA release of rclone v1.35. This is the version that the issue started on.
I was still having this issue with: v1.35-41-g2abfae2
I've now installed v1.35-55-g37fe6d5 and will test accordingly.

OS: RHEL 6 x64 (rclone binary using linux-amd64)

I'm copying from local ext4 filesystem to acd crypt location. It generally works but as of the last week or two I'm uploading and get to 100% and rclone log sits at 100% for a long time and I'll get a gateway timeout. There are a dozen or so files, most are small but there is one large file each day at around 21GB to 22GB.

Script running:
#!/bin/bash
bwlimit=2400

######################################

DATE=`date +%Y%m%d`
SHORTDATE=`date +%y%m%d`

######################################

/usr/local/bin/rclone --config /root/.rclone.conf --include \*$SHORTDATE\* copy /local/dump/ crypt:$DATE --bwlimit $bwlimit -v --no-traverse --max-depth 0



Logs attached in zip.
[rclone_log.zip](https://github.com/ncw/rclone/files/739974/rclone_log.zip)

I looked at issue #902 but it was moved from acd to acd crypt as a culprit. I couldn't seem to find an open case or current forum topic that matched my issue. Could it just be my filesize or something else particular to my selected file list?

issue.title: Seeking files (head, tail etc)

repository.name: rclone
repository.description: "rsync for cloud storage" - Google Drive, S3, Dropbox, Backblaze B2, One Drive, Swift, Hubic, Wasabi, Google Cloud Storage, Azure Blob, Azure Files, Yandex Files

issue.body:
I have a use case where I want to deliberately copy video files from Amazon cloud and seek to end downloading a portion of the beginning and a portion to the end, (zero byte padding in the middle) creating local Linux sparse files. 

```
Amazon:     1G [**********]
My Drive: 100M [**.......*]
```

I know this can be done with the beta via Fuse/seek() but I use a container based VPS provider that that doesn't support loading the Fuse kernel module at the moment. Is it possible for cat/copy to support such a feature to have a specified byte range to download?

body:
I'm facing the same exact issue with uploading large files to Google Drive (60GB). It starts uploading fine and when it gets to around 25% it starts dropping the speed until I get 0 Bytes/s, ETA: 1778029h59m31.770010624s ... any way to debug this?

Edit: With time, it seems the files follow through, but why does it stop for long time at 0 bytes?

@peixotorms it is probably some kind of networking problem.  If it happens again use netstat to work out where rclone is connecting to and then use traceroute to see what the path looks like to those IPs.
I'm going to close this now as the issue is fixed by 2abfae283cd6128cf36bb31bffad1c818e82bbb4
